Saber o número e o nome de cada corda: Know the number and name of each string
Afinar a guitarra com o afinador: Tune the guitar with the tuner
Segurar a guitarra e a palheta sem tensã: Hold the guitar and the pick without tension
Tocar as cordas soltas no pulso do metrô: Play the open strings on the metronome pulse
O que você precisa e como funciona cada: What you need and how each lesson works
Hoje não tem nada para revisar, porque é: Nothing to review today, since it's day one. Get **your guitar, a medium pick** and a place where you can hear your phone or computer. If it's an electric guitar, plug it into an amp or an interface; if you don't have one, you can practice unplugged.
Toda aula tem os mesmos quatro blocos: *: Every lesson has the same four blocks: a **review** of something from earlier days, a **concept**, the **lab** with the metronome, and the **ear** block. Tick each one when you finish it.
Estude todo dia, mesmo que só 15 minutos: Practice every day, even if only for 15 minutes. A little, often, beats a lot, once in a while.
As cordas são numeradas de baixo para ci: The strings are numbered from the bottom up: **string 1** is the thinnest (high sound) and **string 6** is the thickest (low sound). Each open string plays one note, from 6 to 1: **E A D G B E**.
As letras são o jeito internacional de e: Letters are the international way to write notes, and they're what you'll see in chord charts and tabs. To remember the order: **E**ddie **A**te **D**ynamite, **G**ood **B**ye **E**ddie.
No desenho, a corda 1 fica em cima, igua: In the drawing, string 1 is on top, just like you see it looking down at the guitar on your lap. Tab uses the same convention.
Sente na beira da cadeira, com as costas: Sit on the edge of the chair with your back straight. Check each item, ideally in front of a mirror.
A guitarra está apoiada na perna direita: The guitar rests on your right leg
Sentado, sem cruzar as pernas. O braço a: Seated, legs uncrossed. The neck points slightly upward.
Sem dobrar para dentro. Dobra forte cans: Don't bend it inward. A sharp bend gets tiring and causes injuries.
O polegar esquerdo fica atrás do braço: Your left thumb sits behind the neck
Mais ou menos na altura do dedo médio, s: Roughly behind your middle finger, without squeezing.
A palheta está entre o polegar e a later: The pick is between your thumb and the side of your index finger
Só a pontinha aparece. Firme, mas sem es: Only the tip shows. Firm, but don't crush it.
Respire e solte. Tensão aparece primeiro: Breathe and let go. Tension shows up in the shoulders first.
Escolha a corda, toque ela solta e gire: Pick a string, play it open and turn the tuning peg slowly until the needle stops in the middle. Start with string 6 and work up to 1. If the note is way off, use **Hear the right note** for a reference.
Gire a tarraxa aos poucos e toque de nov: Turn the peg a little at a time and play again after each turn. Overtightening snaps the string.
Ligue o metrônomo em `60 BPM`. Toque cad: Set the metronome to `60 BPM`. Play each open string **4 times**, one per click, always with a downstroke. Start on string 6 and finish on 1, without stopping between strings. Count out loud: *1, 2, 3, 4*.
Grave 30 segundos no celular e escute. C: Record 30 seconds on your phone and listen. Does each note land with the click? If so, go up to 70 BPM.
Antes de dar nome às notas, o ouvido pre: Before naming notes, your ear needs to hear direction: did the sound go up or down? Tap **Listen again** to hear two open strings, one after the other, and answer. The goal is 80% right.
Escolha 4 cordas soltas em qualquer orde: Choose 4 open strings in any order and play them on the metronome pulse, repeating the same sequence many times. That's already a riff. Sing along with the notes you're playing.
Saber o que é casa e traste: Know what a fret and a fret wire are
Numerar os dedos da mão esquerda: Number the fingers of the left hand
Tocar o exercício 1-2-3-4 com um dedo po: Play the 1-2-3-4 exercise, one finger per fret
Afine a guitarra, começando pela corda 6: Tune the guitar, starting with string 6. Then say each string's name out loud as you play it: *E, A, D, G, B, E*.
Os **trastes** são as barrinhas de metal: The **fret wires** are the little metal bars across the neck. The space between two wires is the **fret**. When the tab says *fret 3*, press the string in the space between the 2nd and 3rd wire.
Aperte **logo atrás do traste**, não no: Press **right behind the fret wire**, not in the middle of the fret. That way the note rings clean with little effort.
Os dedos da mão esquerda têm números: **: The left-hand fingers have numbers: **1** index, **2** middle, **3** ring, **4** pinky. The thumb is **T**, but it stays behind the neck.
Um dedo por casa: dedo 1 na casa 1, dedo: One finger per fret: finger 1 on fret 1, finger 2 on fret 2, and so on. Tap the dots to hear them.
Toque as casas 1, 2, 3 e 4 em cada corda: Play frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on each string, from 6 to 1, one note per click. Use **one finger per fret** and keep the fingers that already played resting on the string.
O dedo fica logo atrás do traste: The finger sits right behind the fret wire
Nenhuma nota sai abafada ou trastejando: No note comes out muted or buzzing
Trastejar é aquele zumbido de metal. Ape: Buzzing is that metallic rattle. Press a little closer to the fret wire.
Dói na ponta dos dedos? É normal nas pri: Sore fingertips? That's normal in the first weeks. Stop when it hurts and come back later. Calluses show up in about two weeks.
Agora as duas notas ficam a poucas casas: Now the two notes are only a few frets apart. Listen closely: did the second one go up or down?
Diferenciar notas iguais de diferentes: Tell same notes from different ones
Faça o 1-2-3-4 só na corda 1 e na corda: Do the 1-2-3-4 only on strings 1 and 2, slowly, at 60 BPM.
A tablatura tem **6 linhas**, uma para c: Tab has **6 lines**, one per string. The **top line is string 1** (the thinnest), just like the neck drawn in the lessons.
O **número** em cima da linha diz qual c: The **number** on the line tells you which fret to press. **0** is the open string. Read left to right, like text.
Embaixo da tablatura da Pauta aparece o: Below Pauta's tabs you'll see each note's **rhythm**. For now, the black dot with a stem is worth 1 beat (one click). You'll meet the others in the next few days.
A tablatura diz *onde* tocar. A partitur: Tab tells you *where* to play. Standard notation tells you *which note and for how long*. In Pauta the two go together, and notation comes in little by little.
Primeiro leia sozinho, com o metrônomo,: First read it on your own, with the metronome, without listening. Then tap **Play** to check. Use finger 1 on fret 1 and finger 3 on fret 3.
Errou? Siga em frente sem parar. Tocar n: Made a mistake? Keep going without stopping. Playing in time matters more than hitting every note.
Duas notas, uma depois da outra. Elas sã: Two notes, one after the other. Are they the same or different? Sometimes they're only one fret apart.
O pulso e a semínima: The pulse and the quarter note
Ler semínima e pausa de semínima: Read quarter notes and quarter rests
Toque a primeira melodia de ontem. Tente: Play yesterday's first melody. Try it at 70 BPM.
O **pulso** é a batida constante da músi: The **pulse** is the steady beat of the music, the one you tap with your foot. The metronome gives you the pulse, and **BPM** says how many beats per minute.
Beats are grouped into **bars**. In **4/4** each group has 4 beats, and you count *1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4…*. The vertical line in the tab separates the bars.
A **semínima** (bolinha preta com haste): The **quarter note** (black dot with a stem) lasts **1 beat**. The **quarter rest** (the zigzag) is **1 beat of silence**.
Pausa é silêncio de verdade. Encoste a m: A rest is real silence. Rest your right hand on the strings to stop the sound.
Conte em voz alta. Nas pausas, fale o nú: Count out loud. On the rests, say the number more quietly and mute the strings.
Desligue o exemplo e toque só com o metr: Turn off the example and play with just the metronome. Does every note land on the click? Then go up to 70 BPM.
Depois, cante uma nota qualquer e tente: Then sing any note and try to find it on string 1, fret by fret.
Ler mínima (2 tempos) e semibreve (4 tem: Read half notes (2 beats) and whole notes (4 beats)
Segurar a nota até o tempo certo: Hold the note for its full length
Revise as semínimas e pausas de ontem a: Review yesterday's quarter notes and rests at 70 BPM.
A **mínima** é uma bolinha **branca com: The **half note** is a **hollow dot with a stem** and lasts **2 beats**. The **whole note** is a **hollow dot without a stem** and lasts **4 beats**, a whole bar.
1 semibreve = 2 mínimas = 4 semínimas: 1 whole note = 2 half notes = 4 quarter notes
Pausa de mínima: retângulo em cima da li: Half rest: a rectangle sitting on the line (2 beats)
Pausa de semibreve: retângulo pendurado: Whole rest: a rectangle hanging from the line (4 beats)
Tocar uma nota longa é fácil. O difícil: Playing a long note is easy. The hard part is **not letting go early**. Count every beat while the note rings.
Agora com notas presas: use os dedos 1 e: Now with fretted notes: use fingers 1 and 3.
O metrônomo conta um compasso, depois en: The metronome counts one bar, then a note comes in. Did it last 1, 2 or 4 beats?
Sua primeira música: Hino à Alegria: Your first song: Ode to Joy
Achar as notas C, D, E, F e G na primeir: Find the notes C, D, E, F and G in first position
Tocar o Hino à Alegria inteiro: Play the whole Ode to Joy
Afine e toque o exercício de durações de: Tune up and play yesterday's duration exercise.
O Hino à Alegria (Beethoven, 1824) usa s: Ode to Joy (Beethoven, 1824) uses only five notes, all on strings 1 and 2:
Dedo 1 na casa 1, dedo 3 na casa 3. Toqu: Finger 1 on fret 1, finger 3 on fret 3. Play them in order, C, D, E, F, G, and listen to the little staircase going up.
Antes de pegar a guitarra, **cante a mel: Before you pick up the guitar, **sing the melody** on *la-la-la*. If you can sing it, your fingers learn it faster.
Comece com a velocidade em 70% e suba ao: Start with the speed at 70% and go up little by little. Play along with the example, then with just the metronome.
Nos compassos 4 e 8 o ritmo muda: a prim: In bars 4 and 8 the rhythm changes: the first note is longer and the second shorter. No need to count it yet. Listen to the example and copy it.
No hino, cada nota é vizinha da anterior: In the tune, every note is a neighbor of the one before. Play the melody and say out loud whether each note goes up, down or repeats.
Tocar o Hino à Alegria sem parar: Play Ode to Joy without stopping
Afine as seis cordas e diga os nomes em: Tune the six strings and say their names out loud.
Cordas de 1 (aguda) a 6 (grave): E A D G: Strings from 1 (high) to 6 (low): E A D G B E, from 6 to 1
Casa é o espaço entre trastes; aperte lo: A fret is the space between wires; press right behind the wire
Dedos 1 a 4, um dedo por casa: Fingers 1 to 4, one finger per fret
Tablatura: linha de cima = corda 1, núme: Tab: top line = string 1, number = fret
Semínima 1 tempo, mínima 2, semibreve 4: Quarter note 1 beat, half note 2, whole note 4
Afinei as seis cordas em menos de 3 minu: I tuned all six strings in under 3 minutes
Toquei o hino a 60 BPM sem parar: I played the tune at 60 BPM without stopping
Fiz o 1-2-3-4 a 70 BPM sem trastejar: I did the 1-2-3-4 at 70 BPM without buzzing
Montar o Em com as seis cordas soando: Fret Em with all six strings ringing
Play Ode to Joy at 70 BPM.
**Acorde** é um grupo de três ou mais no: A **chord** is a group of three or more notes played together. It's the foundation of almost all accompaniment.
No **diagrama de acorde** a guitarra fic: In a **chord diagram** the guitar stands upright, facing you: the vertical lines are the strings (**6 on the left**), the horizontal ones are the fret wires. The dot shows where to press and the number inside is the finger. **O** on top = open string. **X** = don't play that string.
O Em é o acorde mais fácil da guitarra:: Em is the easiest chord on the guitar: finger 2 on fret 2 of string 5 and finger 3 on fret 2 of string 4. The other strings ring open.
Monte o Em e toque **corda por corda**,: Fret Em and play it **string by string**, from 6 to 1. Every string has to ring.
Os dedos estão na ponta, bem arqueados: My fingers are on their tips, nicely arched
Assim eles não encostam nas cordas vizin: That way they don't touch the neighboring strings.
Cada dedo está logo atrás do traste: Each finger is right behind the fret wire
Quanto mais perto do traste, menos força: The closer to the wire, the less force you need.
Toquei corda por corda e todas soaram: I played string by string and every one rang
Se uma corda morre, descubra qual dedo e: If a string dies, find out which finger is touching it.
Start the strum on the right string.
Agora uma batida para baixo em cada temp: Now one downstroke on each beat, across all six strings.
O Em é um acorde **menor**. Acordes meno: Em is a **minor** chord. Minor chords tend to sound darker, sadder. Major ones sound brighter. Listen and answer.
Lá menor (Am) e a primeira troca: A minor (Am) and your first change
Trocar entre Em e Am no pulso: Change between Em and Am on the pulse
Reconhecer Em e Am de ouvido: Recognize Em and Am by ear
Monte o Em de olhos fechados, abra e con: Fret Em with your eyes closed, open them and check. Repeat 5 times.
Repare na semelhança: os dedos 2 e 3 faz: Notice the resemblance: fingers 2 and 3 make the **same shape as Em, one string over** (strings 4 and 3). Then finger 1 goes on fret 1 of string 2.
No Am a corda 6 tem **X**: comece a bati: Am has an **X** on string 6: start the strum on string 5.
Quatro tempos em cada acorde. No último: Four beats on each chord. On the last beat (yellow), start lifting your fingers toward the next shape.
Troque entre Em e Am o máximo de vezes q: Change between Em and Am as many times as you can in 1 minute, without strumming. Just fret, check and change.
A mão direita: batida no pulso: The right hand: strumming on the pulse
Fazer pausas abafando as cordas: Make rests by muting the strings
A batida sai do **pulso**, não do braço: The strum comes from the **wrist**, not the whole arm. Imagine you're shaking water off your hand.
A mão fica **sempre em movimento**: desc: Your hand is **always moving**: down on the beat, up in the air between beats. That gets everything ready for upstrokes in month 2.
Play **beat 1 a little louder**. That accent helps you (and whoever plays with you) know where the bar starts.
Para fazer pausa com acorde, encoste a l: To rest with a chord, lay the side of your right hand on the strings. The sound stops right away.
Ouvir a diferença entre maior e menor: Hear the difference between major and minor
O D forma um **triângulo** com os dedos: D forms a **triangle** with fingers 1, 2 and 3 on strings 3, 2 and 1. Strings 6 and 5 have an X: the strum starts on **string 4** (open D).
Se a corda 1 não soa, o dedo 3 deve esta: If string 1 doesn't ring, finger 3 is probably lying on it. Arch it more.
Am para D e de volta, o máximo de vezes: Am to D and back, as many times as you can in 1 minute.
O D é **maior**. Compare com o Am e o Em: D is **major**. Compare it with Am and Em, which are minor.
Técnica de troca: forma no ar e último t: Changing technique: shape in the air and the last beat
Montar o acorde inteiro de uma vez: Fret the whole chord at once
Começar a troca no último tempo: Start the change on the last beat
Fret each chord 5 times: Em, Am, D.
**Forma no ar:** levante os dedos juntos: **Shape in the air:** lift your fingers together and land them all at once, like a stamp. Practice the shape 10 times without playing.
**Olhe para frente:** enquanto toca um a: **Look ahead:** while you play one chord, think about the next.
**Último tempo:** a troca começa no temp: **Last beat:** the change starts on beat 4. It's fine if beat 4 comes out with open strings; beat 1 of the next chord has to be right.
Em → Am: os dedos 2 e 3 só descem uma co: Em → Am: fingers 2 and 3 just move down one string together. Feel that move as a single block.
Faça a volta Em → Am → D → Em. Conte qua: Play the round Em → Am → D → Em. Count how many full rounds you do in 1 minute.
Melodia nas cordas graves: Brilha, Brilh: Melody on the low strings: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
Achar C, D, E, F, G e A nas cordas grave: Find C, D, E, F, G and A on the low strings
Até agora as melodias ficaram nas cordas: So far the melodies have stayed on the high strings. Now let's move to strings 5, 4 and 3:
Casa 2 = dedo 2, casa 3 = dedo 3. Toque: Fret 2 = finger 2, fret 3 = finger 3. Play from C up to A.
São as mesmas letras do hino, só que mai: They're the same letters as the Ode, just lower.
Cante a letra enquanto toca. Se o canto: Sing the words while you play. If your voice and the guitar don't match, the note is wrong.
Trocar os três a 60 BPM: Change between the three at 60 BPM
Diagrama: cordas na vertical, a 6 à esqu: Diagram: strings vertical, 6 on the left
Batida com o pulso, acento no 1: Strum from the wrist, accent on 1
Troca: forma no ar e último tempo: Changes: shape in the air and the last beat
Voltas completas Em → Am → D em 1 minuto: Full Em → Am → D rounds in 1 minute. Try to beat your record.
Em, Am e D soam limpos, corda por corda: Em, Am and D ring clean, string by string
Troquei os três a 60 BPM sem parar a bat: I changed between the three at 60 BPM without stopping the strum
Toquei Brilha, Brilha a 70 BPM: I played Twinkle, Twinkle at 70 BPM
Montar o A com três dedos na mesma casa: Fret A with three fingers on the same fret
Ouvir a diferença entre A e Am: Hear the difference between A and Am
O A, e o que muda do Am: A, and what changes from Am
No A, os dedos 1, 2 e 3 ficam todos na *: In A, fingers 1, 2 and 3 all sit on **fret 2**, on strings 4, 3 and 2. It's tight: tilt your fingers a little so they fit.
Compare with Am: **only string 2 changes**. In Am it's on fret 1, in A it's on fret 2. One fret of difference (a half step) turns the chord from sad to happy.
Primeiro A e Am, para ouvir a mudança. D: First A and Am, to hear the change. Then A and D.
Trocar C e Am mantendo dois dedos parado: Change C and Am keeping two fingers still
Reconhecer C, Am e Em de ouvido: Recognize C, Am and Em by ear
O C é uma **escadinha**: dedo 3 na casa: C is a **staircase**: finger 3 on fret 3 of string 5, finger 2 on fret 2 of string 4, finger 1 on fret 1 of string 2. String 6 has an X.
Agora compare com o Am: **os dedos 1 e 2: Now compare with Am: **fingers 1 and 2 are in the same place**. To change, only finger 3 moves, from string 3 to string 5. Fingers that don't need to move, don't.
O dedo 1 costuma encostar na corda 1 e a: Finger 1 tends to touch string 1 and mute it. Arch it well: string 1 has to ring open.
C para Am e de volta, só mexendo o dedo: C to Am and back, moving only finger 3.
Montar o G com o baixo forte: Fret G with a strong bass
O G usa as seis cordas: dedo 2 na casa 3: G uses all six strings: finger 2 on fret 3 of string 6, finger 1 on fret 2 of string 5 and finger 3 on fret 3 of string 1. The middle strings ring open.
O baixo do G (corda 6) é o que dá peso a: G's bass (string 6) is what gives the chord its weight. Start the strum right on it.
Você também vai ver o G com os dedos 3,: You'll also see G fingered with 3, 2 and 4. Both work. Here we use 2, 1 and 3 because it makes getting to C easier later.
G, C e D: a dupla mais famosa ganha um t: G, C and D: the famous pair gets a third
Resolver a troca G → C: Sort out the G → C change
Fret each one 5 times: G, C, D.
Uma **progressão** é uma sequência de ac: A **progression** is a sequence of chords that repeats. **G, C and D** together show up in thousands of rock, country, forró and folk songs. In two months you'll understand why; today is about feeling it in your hands.
A troca mais difícil é **G → C**: os trê: The hardest change is **G → C**: all three fingers change strings. Move your hand as a block, with finger 3 landing first on string 5.
Só a troca G ↔ C, a mais difícil. Quanta: Just the G ↔ C change, the hardest one. How many in 1 minute?
Pausas com acordes: o silêncio também é: Rests with chords: silence is rhythm too
**Mão direita:** encoste a lateral da mã: **Right hand:** lay the side of your hand on the strings, near the bridge.
**Mão esquerda:** alivie a pressão dos d: **Left hand:** ease the finger pressure without lifting them off the strings. Works best with chords without open strings, which you'll learn in month 2.
A rest is a beat like any other. Count out loud: *1, 2, 3, rest*.
Grave um trecho. Nas pausas o som corta: Record a bit. On the rests, does the sound really cut off, or does a trail of the chord linger?
As notas naturais e a escala de Dó: The natural notes and the C scale
Achar as 7 notas naturais na primeira po: Find the 7 natural notes in first position
Ver onde ficam os meios tons: See where the half steps are
Dó, Ré, Mi… no braço: C, D, E… on the neck
As sete notas naturais são **C D E F G A: The seven natural notes are **C D E F G A B** (Do Re Mi Fa Sol La Ti). In first position they sit like this:
Toque de C até C. Isso é a **escala de D: Play from C to C. That's the **C major scale**: Do Re Mi Fa Sol La Ti Do.
Repare nas distâncias. Quase sempre há *: Look at the distances. Almost always there are **two frets** between one note and the next (a whole step). But from **E to F** and from **B to C** the distance is **one fret** (a half step). That difference is what gives the major scale its sound. You'll study it in depth in month 2.
Escala de Dó maior, sobe e desce: C major scale, up and down
Say each note's name as you play.
Trocar G, C, D e Em a 60 BPM: Change G, C, D and Em at 60 BPM
Monte cada acorde e toque corda por cord: Fret each chord and play it string by string.
Seis acordes abertos: Em, Am, D, A, C, G: Six open chords: Em, Am, D, A, C, G
Dedo que não precisa sair, não sai (C ↔: Fingers that don't need to move, don't (C ↔ Am)
Pausas abafando com a mão direita: Rests by muting with the right hand
As 7 notas naturais e a escala de Dó: The 7 natural notes and the C scale
Esta é a sequência do desafio do fim do: This is the end-of-month challenge sequence. Today's goal is 60 BPM.
G → C → D → Em a 60 BPM, duas voltas sem: G → C → D → Em at 60 BPM, two rounds without stopping
Escala de Dó a 70 BPM, falando as notas: C scale at 70 BPM, saying the notes
Levada lenta: G, Em, C, D: Slow strum: G, Em, C, D
Manter o pulso nas trocas: Keep the pulse through the changes
**G → Em → C → D** é a progressão das ba: **G → Em → C → D** is the ballad progression of the '50s and '60s, and it still shows up in a lot of music today. It goes round in a circle: D asks to go back to G.
Comece com **mínimas** (deixe o acorde s: Start with **half notes** (let the chord ring for 2 beats). When you're comfortable, switch to four strums per bar.
Na progressão, só o Em é menor. Escute c: In the progression, only Em is minor. Listen to how it darkens the sound for one bar.
G, D, Em, C: a progressão do pop: G, D, Em, C: the pop progression
Perceber como a ordem muda o clima: Notice how the order changes the mood
Os quatro acordes de ontem, em outra ord: Yesterday's four chords, in a different order: **G → D → Em → C**. This is probably the most used progression in pop over the last few decades. Put it on and sing any melody over it: a lot of things fit.
Ontem o D pedia para voltar ao G. Hoje o: Yesterday D asked to go back to G. Today the C at the end makes the return smoother. The **order** of the chords changes the feeling.
Só a troca D ↔ Em. A mão inteira muda de: Just the D ↔ Em change. Your whole hand moves: think in shapes, not fingers.
Seguir um método para ler música nova: Follow a method to read new music
Tocar sem parar mesmo errando: Play without stopping, even when you slip
**Olhe o ritmo:** onde estão as notas lo: **Look at the rhythm:** where are the long notes and the rests?
**Ache as cordas:** em quais cordas a me: **Find the strings:** which strings does the melody use? Position your hand.
**Conte e cante** a melodia de cabeça, n: **Count and sing** the melody in your head, in time.
**Toque devagar e não pare.** Errou, seg: **Play slowly and don't stop.** Slipped? Keep going. The pulse is the boss.
Nestas melodias, não aperte Tocar antes: For these melodies, don't press Play before trying. Turn on just the metronome (switch off the example after hearing the count-in) and read. Then check against the example.
Maior ou menor: uma nota muda tudo: Major or minor: one note changes everything
Entender que maior e menor diferem por u: Understand that major and minor differ by one note
Você já viu que **A e Am** diferem só na: You've seen that **A and Am** differ only on string 2. **E and Em** are the same: in E, finger 1 goes on fret 1 of string 3. In Em, that string rings open.
Essa nota que muda se chama **terça**. Q: That changing note is called the **third**. When it's one fret higher, the chord is major. One fret lower, minor. In month 3 you'll build chords from this.
Meta de hoje: 80% de acerto em pelo meno: Today's goal: 80% right on at least 10 questions.
Uma corda apertada na **casa 5** dá a me: A string pressed at **fret 5** gives the same note as the next string's open note. For example: string 6 at fret 5 is A, same as open string 5.
Toque cada par: as duas notas têm que se: Play each pair: the two notes have to match. String 3 is the exception, at fret 4. This difference will come up a lot in the course.
Desafine de leve a corda 5. Toque a cord: Slightly detune string 5. Play string 6 at fret 5 and open string 5 together. If they're different, you'll hear **beating**, a *wah-wah-wah*. Turn the peg until the beating disappears.
Faça o mesmo com todas as cordas. Depois: Do the same with every string. Then check with the tuner.
